open_points.subject: ownership and timing of binary-storage environment reads
open_points.text: State 4 says “module:runtime_settings owns reading the environment, once: the closed table config.runtime_environment_variables” and step 1 says load_runtime_settings reads that table; the changed State 3 text says “binary_storage reads BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT and BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES at each binary read”.
open_points.question: After startup, do binary reads use the values captured in RuntimeSettings or re-read the current process environment?
options: Use only the startup RuntimeSettings values
Re-read both variables for every binary read
Use startup values unless a per-read environment value is present
open_points.default_guess: Re-read both variables for every binary read because the new passage calls this an explicit exception.

witness.initial: The service starts with BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT pointing to directory A, and the requested document exists in A; directory B does not contain it.
events: The host operator changes BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT to directory B without restarting the service.
An authorized staff member downloads the document.
outcomes: Following State 4’s read-once boundary, binary_storage uses directory A and returns the document.
Following the changed State 3 exception, binary_storage uses directory B and the document read fails; the staff member receives the concealed document 404.
witness.observer: The staff member downloading the document

open_points.subject: dynamic binary read limit versus startup bound consistency
open_points.text: The changed text says “binary_storage reads BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT and BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES at each binary read”, while A14 says “The storage read bound is checked to be no larger than the declared response ceiling at start” and State 4 says inconsistent binary bounds stop startup.
open_points.question: If BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES changes after startup to exceed the response ceiling validated at startup, which bound governs the read and what outcome is required?
options: Use the new per-read value even when it exceeds the startup response ceiling
Refuse the binary call because the new value violates the bound relationship
Clamp the effective read limit to the startup-validated response ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the binary call when the newly read value exceeds the startup-validated response ceiling.

witness.initial: The service starts with a 10 MB binary read limit and a 10 MB response ceiling; a stored photo is 20 MB.
events: The host operator changes BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES to 30 MB without restarting the service.
An authorized viewer requests the photo.
outcomes: Treating the per-read value as authoritative allows binary_storage to read and return the 20 MB photo.
Preserving the startup consistency requirement refuses the read as storage unavailable, producing the photo-storage 500.
